subproblem.title: Localized Besicovitch density: the excess B ∖ A is relatively small at H^n⌞A-a.e. point
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let U ⊆ ℝ^P be open, and let A ⊆ B ⊆ U be Borel sets with H^n(B ∩ K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U, where H^n := μHE[n]. Then for H^n⌞A-almost every x (∀ᵐ x ∂(μHE[n].restrict A)) the following holds for every extended nonnegative real ε ∈ (0, ∞]: there is ρ_ε > 0 such that H^n((B ∖ A) ∩ B̄_ρ(x)) ≤ ε · H^n(B ∩ B̄_ρ(x)) for all ρ ∈ (0, ρ_ε). Equivalently, the inequality holds eventually in the filter 𝓝[>] 0. Products are taken in [0, ∞] with 0 · ∞ = 0. The exceptional H^n⌞A-null set does not depend on ε.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U A B : Set (Euclid P)), IsOpen U → MeasurableSet A → MeasurableSet B → A ⊆ B → B ⊆ U → (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → μHE[n] (B ∩ K) ≠ ∞) → ∀ᵐ x ∂(μHE[n].restrict A), ∀ ε : ℝ≥0∞, 0 < ε → ∀ᶠ ρ in 𝓝[>] (0 : ℝ), μHE[n] ((B \ A) ∩ closedBall x ρ) ≤ ε * μHE[n] (B ∩ closedBall x ρ)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps 2–4 of the parent-supplied proof. These implement Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.5(2) and the proof of Theorem 1.6 "⇒" (chapter-03.txt lines 87–90 and 113–143). Simon's Upper Density Theorem is replaced by the Besicovitch density theorem: Simon Ch. 1, Theorem 3.16, which is Mathlib's Besicovitch.ae_tendsto_measure_inter_div.
Notation:
- E := Euclid P = ℝ^P, H^n := μHE[n], μ_A := H^n⌞A = μHE[n].restrict A;
- B̄_ρ(z), B_ρ(z) are the closed and open balls.
Measures of sets lie in [0, ∞], where a/b := a·b⁻¹ with 0⁻¹ = ∞ and ∞⁻¹ = 0; in particular 0/b = 0 for every b.
1. Countable cover. E is a separable metric space; let D ⊆ E be a countable dense set. Let 𝒦 be the family of closed balls B̄_s(q) with q ∈ D, s ∈ ℚ, s > 0 and B̄_s(q) ⊆ U.
- 𝒦 is countable, since it is indexed by a subset of D × ℚ.
- Each K ∈ 𝒦 is closed and bounded in the finite-dimensional space E, hence compact (isCompact_closedBall), and K ⊆ U. So H^n(B ∩ K) < ∞ by hypothesis.
- Every z ∈ U lies in the open ball B_s(q) of some B̄_s(q) ∈ 𝒦. Since U is open, choose δ > 0 with B_δ(z) ⊆ U. Choose q ∈ D with |z − q| < δ/4 and a rational s ∈ (δ/4, δ/2). Then |z − q| < s. If |y − q| ≤ s, then |y − z| ≤ s + δ/4 < δ, so B̄_s(q) ⊆ B_δ(z) ⊆ U.
Only these three properties are used below. Any countable family of closed balls inside U whose open balls cover U works equally well, e.g. one obtained from second countability via TopologicalSpace.countable_cover_nhdsWithin.
2. Besicovitch density on one ball. Fix K ∈ 𝒦 and put ν_K := H^n⌞(B ∩ K) = μHE[n].restrict (B ∩ K).
- ν_K(E) = H^n(B ∩ K) < ∞, so ν_K is a finite, hence locally finite, Borel measure on E.
- E is a finite-dimensional real normed space, so it is second countable and has the Besicovitch covering property (instHasBesicovitchCovering).
- By the Besicovitch density theorem (Besicovitch.ae_tendsto_measure_inter_div ν_K A), for ν_K⌞A-a.e. z we have
 Conv_K(z): ν_K(A ∩ B̄_ρ(z)) / ν_K(B̄_ρ(z)) → 1 in [0, ∞] as ρ → 0 in 𝓝[>] 0.
- A, B and K are Borel and A ⊆ B. Applying Measure.restrict_restrict twice gives ν_K⌞A = H^n⌞(A ∩ B ∩ K) = H^n⌞(A ∩ K) = (μ_A)⌞K.
- Hence Conv_K(z) holds for (μ_A)⌞K-a.e. z. Since K is Borel, ae_restrict_iff' turns this into: for μ_A-a.e. z, z ∈ K ⇒ Conv_K(z).
3. One exceptional set. 𝒦 is countable, so the countably many μ_A-a.e. statements of step 2 hold simultaneously (ae_ball_iff): for μ_A-a.e. z, Conv_K(z) holds for every K ∈ 𝒦 with z ∈ K. Moreover μ_A-a.e. z lies in A (ae_restrict_mem, A Borel). Let N be the μ_A-null set where either property fails. N depends on n, U, A and B, but not on ε.
4. Local form of the ratio. Fix x ∉ N.
- x ∈ A ⊆ B ⊆ U, so by step 1 there is K = B̄_s(q) ∈ 𝒦 with x ∈ B_s(q). Put ρ₀ := s − |x − q| > 0.
- For 0 < ρ < ρ₀ and |y − x| ≤ ρ we have |y − q| ≤ ρ + |x − q| < s. So B̄_ρ(x) ⊆ B_s(q) ⊆ K.
- As x ∈ K and x ∉ N, Conv_K(x) holds.
Write a(ρ) := H^n(A ∩ B̄_ρ(x)), β(ρ) := H^n(B ∩ B̄_ρ(x)) and e(ρ) := H^n((B ∖ A) ∩ B̄_ρ(x)). For 0 < ρ < ρ₀:
(i) ν_K(A ∩ B̄_ρ(x)) = H^n(A ∩ B̄_ρ(x) ∩ B ∩ K) = a(ρ), since A ⊆ B and B̄_ρ(x) ⊆ K;
(ii) ν_K(B̄_ρ(x)) = H^n(B̄_ρ(x) ∩ B ∩ K) = β(ρ), since B̄_ρ(x) ⊆ K;
(iii) β(ρ) ≤ H^n(B ∩ K) < ∞.
The interval (0, ρ₀) belongs to 𝓝[>] 0. On it the quotient in Conv_K(x) equals a(ρ)/β(ρ) by (i)–(ii), so a(ρ)/β(ρ) → 1 as ρ → 0 in 𝓝[>] 0.
(iv) For every ρ, e(ρ) + a(ρ) = β(ρ). The sets (B ∖ A) ∩ B̄_ρ(x) and A ∩ B̄_ρ(x) are disjoint, the second is Borel, and their union is B ∩ B̄_ρ(x) because A ⊆ B (measure_union).
5. The estimate. Let ε ∈ (0, ∞].
(a) Case ε ≥ 1. For every ρ, monotonicity ((B ∖ A) ∩ B̄_ρ(x) ⊆ B ∩ B̄_ρ(x)) gives e(ρ) ≤ β(ρ) = 1 · β(ρ) ≤ ε · β(ρ). So the bound holds for all ρ, in particular eventually.
(b) Case ε < 1. Then 1 − ε < 1 (truncated subtraction in [0, ∞]; ε > 0 and 1 ≠ ∞), so (1 − ε, ∞] is a neighbourhood of 1. Since a(ρ)/β(ρ) → 1, there is ρ_ε ∈ (0, ρ₀] such that a(ρ)/β(ρ) > 1 − ε for all ρ ∈ (0, ρ_ε). Fix such a ρ.
- β(ρ) ≠ 0. Otherwise a(ρ) ≤ β(ρ) = 0 by (iv), so a(ρ)/β(ρ) = 0/0 = 0, contradicting a(ρ)/β(ρ) > 1 − ε ≥ 0.
- β(ρ) ≠ ∞ by (iii).
- Since 0 < β(ρ) < ∞, the inequality a(ρ)/β(ρ) > 1 − ε is equivalent to (1 − ε)·β(ρ) < a(ρ) (ENNReal.lt_div_iff_mul_lt).
- Since ε ≤ 1, ε + (1 − ε) = 1. Hence
 e(ρ) + (1 − ε)β(ρ) ≤ e(ρ) + a(ρ) = β(ρ) = ε·β(ρ) + (1 − ε)·β(ρ).
- (1 − ε)β(ρ) < ∞ can be cancelled (ENNReal.le_of_add_le_add_right), giving e(ρ) ≤ ε·β(ρ).
In both cases e(ρ) ≤ ε·β(ρ) holds for all ρ in an interval (0, ρ_ε), that is, eventually in 𝓝[>] 0.
6. Conclusion. Every x ∉ N satisfies the eventual estimate of step 5 for every ε ∈ (0, ∞]. N is μ_A-null and independent of ε, which is the claim. If U = ∅ then A = ∅ and μ_A = 0, so the claim is vacuous; the argument above covers this case as well. ∎
proof_key_steps: A countable family 𝒦 of closed balls B̄_s(q) ⊆ U (compact, so H^n(B ∩ K) < ∞) whose open balls cover U.
Besicovitch density for ν_K = H^n⌞(B ∩ K) holds at ν_K⌞A = (H^n⌞A)⌞K-a.e. point, hence for H^n⌞A-a.e. z ∈ K.
Countable intersection gives one H^n⌞A-null set N, independent of ε, off which x ∈ A and every relevant density ratio tends to 1.
For x ∉ N and small ρ: H^n(A ∩ B̄_ρ)/H^n(B ∩ B̄_ρ) → 1, H^n(B ∩ B̄_ρ) < ∞, and e + a = β.
If ε ≥ 1, monotonicity gives e ≤ εβ. If ε < 1, ratio > 1 − ε forces 0 < β < ∞ and (1 − ε)β < a; cancelling gives e ≤ εβ.

audit.reason: All hypotheses and the placement of ∀ ε inside the a.e. conclusion match. The countable compact cover and localized finite-measure density theorem produce one exceptional set. Restriction identities and finite ENNReal cancellation justify the estimate, including zero denominators and ε = ∞. The proof is complete and independent of the parent.

subproblem.title: Hausdorff-measure scaling under the blow-up map
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, x ∈ ℝ^P, r, R ∈ ℝ with r > 0, and let S ⊆ ℝ^P be an arbitrary set. Let η := η_{x,r} be SimonGMT's blowUpMap x r, η(z) = r⁻¹(z − x), and let H^n := μHE[n] (Mathlib's Euclidean Hausdorff measure on Euclid P = ℝ^P). Then H^n(η(S) ∩ B̄_R(0)) = ((ENNReal.ofReal r)⁻¹)^n · H^n(S ∩ B̄_{r·R}(x)), where B̄ denotes closed balls and the product is taken in [0, ∞].
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (x : Euclid P) (r R : ℝ) (S : Set (Euclid P)), 0 < r → μHE[n] (Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.blowUpMap x r '' S ∩ closedBall 0 R) = (ENNReal.ofReal r)⁻¹ ^ n * μHE[n] (S ∩ closedBall x (r * R))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 1 of the parent-supplied proof (blow-up scaling), the scaling fact used in Simon Ch. 3, proof of Theorem 1.6 "⇒" (chapter-03.txt lines 113–143). Notation: E := Euclid P = ℝ^P, H^n := μHE[n], η := blowUpMap x r, so η(z) = r⁻¹ • (z − x).
1. Norm of the blow-up. For z ∈ E, ‖η(z)‖ = |r⁻¹|·‖z − x‖ = r⁻¹‖z − x‖, because r > 0.
2. Set identity η(S) ∩ B̄_R(0) = η(S ∩ B̄_{rR}(x)).
(⊆) Let y ∈ η(S) ∩ B̄_R(0), so y = η(z) with z ∈ S. Then r⁻¹‖z − x‖ = ‖y‖ ≤ R. Multiplying by r > 0 gives dist(z, x) = ‖z − x‖ ≤ rR. So z ∈ S ∩ B̄_{rR}(x) and y = η(z).
(⊇) Let z ∈ S ∩ B̄_{rR}(x). Then ‖η(z)‖ = r⁻¹‖z − x‖ ≤ r⁻¹(rR) = R, so η(z) ∈ η(S) ∩ B̄_R(0).
If R < 0, both sides are empty, and the argument above covers this case.
3. Factorization. Let h := AffineMap.homothety x r⁻¹, so h(z) = x + r⁻¹ • (z − x), and let τ(y) := y + (−x) be the translation by −x. Then τ(h(z)) = r⁻¹ • (z − x) = η(z) for every z. Thus η = τ ∘ h, and η(T) = τ(h(T)) for every T ⊆ E.
4. Scaling of H^n under η. Let T ⊆ E be arbitrary.
- τ is an isometry (isometry_add_right), so H^n(τ(W)) = H^n(W) for every W (Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image).
- h is a homothety of ratio r⁻¹ ≠ 0, so H^n(h(T)) = ‖r⁻¹‖₊^n • H^n(T) (MeasureTheory.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_homothety_image).
- ‖r⁻¹‖₊ = ‖r‖₊⁻¹ (nnnorm_inv), and ‖r‖₊ = Real.toNNReal r ≠ 0 because r > 0 (Real.nnnorm_of_nonneg). Coercion to [0, ∞] commutes with the inverse of a nonzero element (ENNReal.coe_inv) and with powers (ENNReal.coe_pow), and ↑(Real.toNNReal r) = ENNReal.ofReal r. Hence the factor ‖r⁻¹‖₊^n, viewed in [0, ∞], equals ((ENNReal.ofReal r)⁻¹)^n.
Consequently H^n(η(T)) = H^n(τ(h(T))) = H^n(h(T)) = ((ENNReal.ofReal r)⁻¹)^n · H^n(T).
5. Conclusion. Apply step 2, then step 4 with T := S ∩ B̄_{rR}(x):
H^n(η(S) ∩ B̄_R(0)) = H^n(η(S ∩ B̄_{rR}(x))) = ((ENNReal.ofReal r)⁻¹)^n · H^n(S ∩ B̄_{rR}(x)).
No measurability of S is needed: steps 2–4 are identities of sets and of the measure H^n evaluated on arbitrary sets. ∎
proof_key_steps: ‖η_{x,r}(z)‖ = r⁻¹‖z − x‖ because r > 0.
Set identity η(S) ∩ B̄_R(0) = η(S ∩ B̄_{rR}(x)).
η = (translation by −x) ∘ (homothety with centre x and ratio r⁻¹).
H^n(η(T)) = ‖r⁻¹‖₊^n H^n(T) = ((ofReal r)⁻¹)^n H^n(T), by isometry invariance and homothety scaling of μHE[n].
Combine the set identity with the scaling for T = S ∩ B̄_{rR}(x).

audit.reason: The prose and standalone one-line type agree, including arbitrary S and unrestricted R. The ball-image identity, nonzero homothety scaling and translation invariance prove the precise ENNReal factor without measurability assumptions. Negative R and n = 0 are covered. No circular reliance occurs.

subproblem.title: Zero n-density of the excess from a growth bound and relative smallness
subproblem.statement:
Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let A, B ⊆ ℝ^P be arbitrary sets, x ∈ ℝ^P, and r₀, C, r₁ ∈ ℝ with r₀ > 0, r₁ > 0 and H^n(B ∩ B̄_{r₀}(x)) < ∞, where H^n := μHE[n]. Assume:
(G) H^n(A ∩ B̄_ρ(x)) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal(C · ρ^n) for all ρ ∈ (0, r₁);
(E) for every extended nonnegative real ε ∈ (0, ∞], eventually as ρ → 0 in 𝓝[>] 0, H^n((B ∖ A) ∩ B̄_ρ(x)) ≤ ε · H^n(B ∩ B̄_ρ(x)).
Then H^n((B ∖ A) ∩ B̄_ρ(x)) / (ENNReal.ofReal ρ)^n → 0 in [0, ∞] as ρ → 0 in 𝓝[>] 0, where the quotient is taken in [0, ∞] (a/b = a·b⁻¹).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (A B : Set (Euclid P)) (x : Euclid P) (r₀ C r₁ : ℝ), 0 < r₀ → μHE[n] (B ∩ closedBall x r₀) ≠ ∞ → 0 < r₁ → (∀ ρ : ℝ, 0 < ρ → ρ < r₁ → μHE[n] (A ∩ closedBall x ρ) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (C * ρ ^ n)) → (∀ ε : ℝ≥0∞, 0 < ε → ∀ᶠ ρ in 𝓝[>] (0 : ℝ), μHE[n] ((B \ A) ∩ closedBall x ρ) ≤ ε * μHE[n] (B ∩ closedBall x ρ)) → Tendsto (fun ρ : ℝ => μHE[n] ((B \ A) ∩ closedBall x ρ) / ENNReal.ofReal ρ ^ n) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 0)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 6 of the parent-supplied proof (zero n-density of the excess).
Notation: H^n := μHE[n]. In [0, ∞] put
- a(ρ) := H^n(A ∩ B̄_ρ(x)), β(ρ) := H^n(B ∩ B̄_ρ(x)), e(ρ) := H^n((B ∖ A) ∩ B̄_ρ(x));
- c := ENNReal.ofReal C ∈ [0, ∞) and κ := 2c ∈ [0, ∞).
1. Rewriting (G). For ρ > 0 we have ρ^n ≥ 0, so ENNReal.ofReal(C·ρ^n) = ofReal(C)·ofReal(ρ^n) = c·(ofReal ρ)^n (ENNReal.ofReal_mul', ENNReal.ofReal_pow). Thus a(ρ) ≤ c·(ofReal ρ)^n for ρ ∈ (0, r₁).
2. Doubling bound for B. Claim: eventually in 𝓝[>] 0, β(ρ) ≤ κ·(ofReal ρ)^n.
The interval (0, min(r₀, r₁)) belongs to 𝓝[>] 0, and (E) with ε = 1/2 holds eventually; so the conjunction holds eventually. Let ρ satisfy both. Then:
- β(ρ) ≤ H^n(B ∩ B̄_{r₀}(x)) < ∞ by monotonicity, since ρ ≤ r₀;
- β(ρ) ≤ a(ρ) + e(ρ) by monotonicity and subadditivity, since B ∩ B̄_ρ(x) ⊆ (A ∩ B̄_ρ(x)) ∪ ((B ∖ A) ∩ B̄_ρ(x)); no relation between A and B is needed;

Hence β/2 + β/2 = β ≤ a + e ≤ a + β/2. Since β/2 < ∞ it can be cancelled, so β(ρ)/2 ≤ a(ρ). Therefore, using step 1 (ρ < r₁),
 β(ρ) = β/2 + β/2 ≤ 2·a(ρ) ≤ 2c·(ofReal ρ)^n = κ·(ofReal ρ)^n.
3. Smallness. We use ENNReal.tendsto_nhds_zero: g(ρ) → 0 in [0, ∞] iff for every δ ∈ (0, ∞], eventually g(ρ) ≤ δ.
Let δ > 0. If δ = ∞ there is nothing to prove. Otherwise δ ∈ (0, ∞); put ε := δ/(κ + 1). As κ + 1 ∈ [1, ∞), ε ∈ (0, ∞). Eventually both step 2 and (E) with this ε hold. For such ρ:
 e(ρ) ≤ ε·β(ρ) ≤ ε·(κ + 1)·(ofReal ρ)^n = δ·(ofReal ρ)^n.
The middle inequality uses β ≤ κ·(ofReal ρ)^n ≤ (κ + 1)·(ofReal ρ)^n. The last equality uses (δ/(κ + 1))·(κ + 1) = δ, valid because κ + 1 ∉ {0, ∞}. Then e(ρ)/(ofReal ρ)^n ≤ δ (ENNReal.div_le_of_le_mul).
4. Conclusion. e(ρ)/(ofReal ρ)^n → 0 as ρ → 0 in 𝓝[>] 0.
- For n = 0 all powers equal 1 and the argument is unchanged.
- If C < 0 then c = 0 and the argument is unchanged. ∎

subproblem.title: Zero-density excess does not change approximate tangent spaces (Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.5(2), pointwise form)
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let A ⊆ B ⊆ ℝ^P be Borel sets, x ∈ ℝ^P and r₀ > 0 with H^n(B ∩ B̄_{r₀}(x)) < ∞, where H^n := μHE[n]. Suppose (†) H^n((B ∖ A) ∩ B̄_ρ(x)) / (ENNReal.ofReal ρ)^n → 0 in [0, ∞] as ρ → 0 in 𝓝[>] 0, the quotient taken in [0, ∞] (a/b = a·b⁻¹). Then for every linear subspace Q of ℝ^P, B has approximate tangent space Q at x (HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n B x Q, Simon Ch. 3, Definition 1.4) if and only if A has approximate tangent space Q at x.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (A B : Set (Euclid P)) (x : Euclid P) (r₀ : ℝ), MeasurableSet A → MeasurableSet B → A ⊆ B → 0 < r₀ → μHE[n] (B ∩ closedBall x r₀) ≠ ∞ → Tendsto (fun ρ : ℝ => μHE[n] ((B \ A) ∩ closedBall x ρ) / ENNReal.ofReal ρ ^ n) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 0) → ∀ Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P), HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n B x Q ↔ HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n A x Q
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 7 and the transfer part of step 8 of the parent-supplied proof. These follow Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.5(2) and the proof of Theorem 1.6 "⇒" (chapter-03.txt lines 87–90 and 113–143), which bounds |∫_{η(M∖N_j)} f| by sup|f|·ρ^{−n}·H^n(B_{ρR}(x) ∩ M ∖ N_j).
Definition: HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n S x Q means finrank Q = n and, for every f ∈ C_c(E, ℝ), ∫_{η_ρ(S)} f dH^n → ∫_Q f dH^n as ρ → 0 in 𝓝[>] 0. These are Bochner integrals for μHE[n] restricted to the set; a non-integrable integrand has integral 0.
Notation: E := Euclid P = ℝ^P, H^n := μHE[n], η_ρ := blowUpMap x ρ, so η_ρ(z) = ρ⁻¹(z − x).
We use the sibling lemma blowup_scaling: for ρ > 0, R ∈ ℝ and S ⊆ E,
 H^n(η_ρ(S) ∩ B̄_R(0)) = ((ofReal ρ)⁻¹)^n · H^n(S ∩ B̄_{ρR}(x)).
1. Blow-up maps. Let ρ ≠ 0.
- η_ρ is injective: ρ⁻¹(a − x) = ρ⁻¹(b − x) implies a = b.
- For every Borel S ⊆ E, η_ρ(S) = {y : x + ρy ∈ S}. This is the preimage of S under the continuous map y ↦ x + ρy, hence Borel.
2. Key claim: for every f ∈ C_c(E, ℝ),
 Δ_f(ρ) := ∫_{η_ρ(B)} f dH^n − ∫_{η_ρ(A)} f dH^n → 0 as ρ → 0 in 𝓝[>] 0.
Fix f.
(a) Bounds on f. tsupport f is compact, hence bounded, so tsupport f ⊆ B̄_{R₀}(0) for some R₀. Put R := max(R₀, 1) > 0; then f(y) = 0 for y ∉ B̄_R(0). Also f is continuous with compact support, hence bounded: |f| ≤ M for some real M.
(b) Integrability criterion. Let S ⊆ E with H^n(S ∩ B̄_R(0)) < ∞. Then f is H^n-integrable on S. Indeed f is measurable and |f| ≤ M·1_{B̄_R(0)}, which is integrable for H^n⌞S because (H^n⌞S)(B̄_R(0)) = H^n(S ∩ B̄_R(0)) < ∞.
(c) Finiteness. Fix ρ with 0 < ρ < r₀/R, so ρR < r₀. For every S ⊆ B, blowup_scaling gives
 H^n(η_ρ(S) ∩ B̄_R(0)) = ((ofReal ρ)⁻¹)^n · H^n(S ∩ B̄_{ρR}(x)) ≤ ((ofReal ρ)⁻¹)^n · H^n(B ∩ B̄_{r₀}(x)) < ∞.
(d) Splitting. By injectivity, η_ρ(B ∖ A) = η_ρ(B) ∖ η_ρ(A). Also η_ρ(A) ⊆ η_ρ(B), η_ρ(A) is Borel by step 1, and f is integrable on η_ρ(B) by (b) and (c) with S = B. Hence Δ_f(ρ) = ∫_{η_ρ(B ∖ A)} f dH^n (setIntegral_sdiff).
(e) Estimate.
- η_ρ(B ∖ A) is Borel, since B ∖ A is Borel (step 1).
- f = 0 on η_ρ(B ∖ A) ∖ B̄_R(0), so ∫_{η_ρ(B∖A)} f = ∫_{η_ρ(B∖A) ∩ B̄_R(0)} f (setIntegral_eq_of_subset_of_forall_sdiff_eq_zero).
- The set η_ρ(B ∖ A) ∩ B̄_R(0) has finite measure by (c) with S = B ∖ A, and |f| ≤ M on it.
- Hence |Δ_f(ρ)| ≤ M·m(ρ), where m(ρ) := (H^n(η_ρ(B ∖ A) ∩ B̄_R(0))).toReal (norm_setIntegral_le_of_norm_le_const).
(f) The bound tends to 0.
- Since R > 0, the map ρ ↦ ρR is continuous, vanishes at 0 and is positive for ρ > 0, so it sends 𝓝[>] 0 to 𝓝[>] 0.
- For ρ > 0, ofReal(ρR)^n = (ofReal ρ)^n·(ofReal R)^n with (ofReal R)^n ∈ (0, ∞). So by blowup_scaling
 H^n(η_ρ(B ∖ A) ∩ B̄_R(0)) = ((ofReal ρ)⁻¹)^n · H^n((B ∖ A) ∩ B̄_{ρR}(x)) = (ofReal R)^n · [H^n((B ∖ A) ∩ B̄_{ρR}(x)) / (ofReal(ρR))^n].
- By (†) composed with ρ ↦ ρR, the bracket tends to 0. The constant (ofReal R)^n is finite, so H^n(η_ρ(B ∖ A) ∩ B̄_R(0)) → (ofReal R)^n · 0 = 0 in [0, ∞] (ENNReal.Tendsto.const_mul).
- toReal is continuous at 0 (ENNReal.tendsto_toReal), so m(ρ) → 0 and M·m(ρ) → 0.
- By (e), |Δ_f(ρ)| ≤ M·m(ρ) for all ρ ∈ (0, r₀/R), a set in 𝓝[>] 0. The squeeze theorem (squeeze_zero_norm') gives Δ_f(ρ) → 0.
For n = 0 all powers equal 1.
3. (⇒) Suppose HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n B x Q: finrank Q = n, and ∫_{η_ρ(B)} f → ∫_Q f for every f ∈ C_c. By step 2, ∫_{η_ρ(A)} f = ∫_{η_ρ(B)} f − Δ_f(ρ) → ∫_Q f − 0 = ∫_Q f. Together with finrank Q = n, A has approximate tangent space Q at x.
4. (⇐) Suppose HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n A x Q. By step 2, ∫_{η_ρ(B)} f = ∫_{η_ρ(A)} f + Δ_f(ρ) → ∫_Q f + 0 for every f. Together with finrank Q = n, B has approximate tangent space Q at x. ∎
proof_key_steps: η_ρ is injective and maps Borel sets to Borel sets (preimage under y ↦ x + ρy).
For f ∈ C_c vanishing off B̄_R(0) with |f| ≤ M, f is integrable on η_ρ(B) for 0 < ρ < r₀/R (blowup_scaling plus finiteness).
∫_{η_ρ(B)} f − ∫_{η_ρ(A)} f = ∫_{η_ρ(B∖A) ∩ B̄_R(0)} f, bounded by M·H^n(η_ρ(B∖A) ∩ B̄_R(0)).
blowup_scaling: H^n(η_ρ(B∖A) ∩ B̄_R(0)) = R^n·(ρR)^{−n} H^n((B∖A) ∩ B̄_{ρR}(x)) → 0 by (†).
Transfer the blow-up limits in both directions; finrank Q = n is common to both sides.

subproblem.title: Growth bound from an approximate tangent plane (Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.5(3))
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let D ⊆ ℝ^P be a Borel set, x ∈ ℝ^P, Q a linear subspace of ℝ^P, and r₀ > 0 with H^n(D ∩ B̄_{r₀}(x)) < ∞, where H^n := μHE[n]. Suppose D has approximate tangent space Q at x (HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n D x Q). That is, finrank Q = n and, for every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P, ℝ), ∫_{η_{x,r}(D)} f dH^n → ∫_Q f dH^n as r → 0 in 𝓝[>] 0. Then there are real numbers C and r₁ with r₁ > 0 such that H^n(D ∩ B̄_ρ(x)) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal(C · ρ^n) for all ρ ∈ (0, r₁).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (D : Set (Euclid P)) (x : Euclid P) (Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)) (r₀ : ℝ), MeasurableSet D → 0 < r₀ → μHE[n] (D ∩ closedBall x r₀) ≠ ∞ → HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n D x Q → ∃ C r₁ : ℝ, 0 < r₁ ∧ ∀ ρ : ℝ, 0 < ρ → ρ < r₁ → μHE[n] (D ∩ closedBall x ρ) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (C * ρ ^ n)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 5 of the parent-supplied proof, i.e. Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.5(3) (chapter-03.txt lines 91–95). Testing Definition 1.4 with a cutoff that equals 1 on B_1(0) bounds the density ratio.
Notation: E := Euclid P = ℝ^P, H^n := μHE[n], η_ρ := blowUpMap x ρ (so η_ρ(z) = ρ⁻¹(z − x)). Integrals are Bochner integrals.
We use the sibling lemma blowup_scaling: for ρ > 0, R ∈ ℝ and any S ⊆ E,
 H^n(η_ρ(S) ∩ B̄_R(0)) = ((ENNReal.ofReal ρ)⁻¹)^n · H^n(S ∩ B̄_{ρR}(x)).
1. Test function. Let φ(w) := max(0, min(1, 2 − ‖w‖)).
- φ is continuous.
- If ‖w‖ > 2 then 2 − ‖w‖ < 0, so φ(w) = 0. Hence φ vanishes outside the compact ball B̄_2(0), and φ is an element of C_c(E, ℝ) (HasCompactSupport.intro with isCompact_closedBall).
- 0 ≤ φ ≤ 1 everywhere, and φ(w) = 1 when ‖w‖ ≤ 1 (then 2 − ‖w‖ ≥ 1).
2. Choice of C and r₁. Let Λ := ∫_Q φ dH^n ∈ ℝ and C := |Λ| + 1.
- The second component of the tangent hypothesis, with f := φ, gives I(ρ) := ∫_{η_ρ(D)} φ dH^n → Λ as ρ → 0 in 𝓝[>] 0.
- Since Λ ≤ |Λ| < C, eventually I(ρ) < C (Tendsto.eventually_lt_const).
- Also eventually ρ < r₀/2, because (0, r₀/2) ∈ 𝓝[>] 0.
- The conjunction holds eventually in 𝓝[>] 0. By mem_nhdsGT_iff_exists_Ioo_subset there is r₁ > 0 such that every ρ ∈ (0, r₁) satisfies I(ρ) < C and ρ < r₀/2.
3. Finiteness near the origin. Fix ρ ∈ (0, r₁) and put T := η_ρ(D). By blowup_scaling with R = 2,
 H^n(T ∩ B̄_2(0)) = ((ENNReal.ofReal ρ)⁻¹)^n · H^n(D ∩ B̄_{2ρ}(x)).
The first factor is finite because ρ > 0. The second is at most H^n(D ∩ B̄_{r₀}(x)) < ∞, because 2ρ < r₀. Hence H^n(T ∩ B̄_2(0)) < ∞.
4. Integrability. φ is continuous, hence strongly measurable. Pointwise |φ| ≤ 1_{B̄_2(0)}, because φ ≤ 1 and φ = 0 off B̄_2(0). The indicator 1_{B̄_2(0)} is integrable for H^n⌞T, since B̄_2(0) is Borel and (H^n⌞T)(B̄_2(0)) = H^n(T ∩ B̄_2(0)) < ∞. So φ is integrable for H^n⌞T (Integrable.mono').
5. Comparison with the test integral. Pointwise 1_{B̄_1(0)} ≤ φ, since φ = 1 on B̄_1(0) and φ ≥ 0 elsewhere. Hence
 H^n(T ∩ B̄_1(0)) = ∫⁻ 1_{B̄_1(0)} d(H^n⌞T) ≤ ∫⁻ ofReal(φ) d(H^n⌞T) = ofReal(∫ φ d(H^n⌞T)) = ofReal(I(ρ)) ≤ ofReal(C).
This uses lintegral_indicator_one, lintegral_mono, ofReal_integral_eq_lintegral_ofReal (φ is integrable and ≥ 0), and I(ρ) < C.
6. Rescaling back. By blowup_scaling with R = 1 (ρ · 1 = ρ),
 H^n(T ∩ B̄_1(0)) = ((ENNReal.ofReal ρ)⁻¹)^n · H^n(D ∩ B̄_ρ(x)).
Now ((ofReal ρ)⁻¹)^n = ((ofReal ρ)^n)⁻¹ and (ofReal ρ)^n ∈ (0, ∞). Multiplying by (ofReal ρ)^n gives
 H^n(D ∩ B̄_ρ(x)) = (ofReal ρ)^n · H^n(T ∩ B̄_1(0)) ≤ (ofReal ρ)^n · ofReal(C) = ofReal(C · ρ^n).
The last equality is ofReal(C·ρ^n) = ofReal(C)·ofReal(ρ)^n, valid since C ≥ 0 and ρ ≥ 0 (ENNReal.ofReal_mul, ENNReal.ofReal_pow).
7. Conclusion. C = |Λ| + 1 and r₁ from step 2 satisfy the claim. The Borel hypothesis on D is not used. ∎
proof_key_steps: The tangent hypothesis gives ∫_{η_ρ(D)} φ → Λ := ∫_Q φ; choose r₁ with ∫_{η_ρ(D)} φ < |Λ| + 1 and ρ < r₀/2 on (0, r₁).
blowup_scaling (R = 2) gives H^n(η_ρ(D) ∩ B̄_2(0)) < ∞, so φ is integrable on η_ρ(D).
blowup_scaling (R = 1) gives H^n(D ∩ B̄_ρ(x)) = ρ^n H^n(η_ρ(D) ∩ B̄_1(0)) ≤ (|Λ| + 1)ρ^n.

The unused Borel hypothesis is harmless. The declared dependency is correct.
